Abigail Thompson Rangeley Lakes Regional School LD 360
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education, I am writing to voice my support for LD 360.
I am the PK-12 School Librarian at the Rangeley Lakes Regional School in Rangeley, ME and coordinate the distribution of the Dirigo Reads book to our first graders. Over the past four years of participation in this program, every single first grade student looks forward to their new books and are thrilled to explore, read, and share their "books to keep". Receiving a new book every month (or every other month as the case has been for the 24-25 school year) gives students something personal and tangible to connect them to reading. For many students, these books open doors to worlds they might not otherwise have explored, engaging their curiosity and sparking imagination.
Dirigo Reads helps ensure that every child, regardless of background or financial circumstance, has access to high quality, age-relevant books. We all know the stats about the critical importance of reading to children throughout their earliest years, that access to books in the home is the single biggest indicator of academic success, and more. The Dirigo Reads program helps to address those gaps by building a mini library for first grade students, a time when many students unlock reading. Living in a rural corner of the state, many RLRS students do not have easy access to the local public library, and access to a bookstore is even more limited. Thanks to Dirigo Reads, students have equitable access to the type of books which help them build essential reading skills, support them in becoming confident readers, and develop a lifelong love of books and reading which will serve them for years to come.
Thank you for supporting this essential program.
Abigail Thompson PK-12 School Librarian/Media Specialist Rangeley Lakes Regional School Resident of Rangeley, ME

Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education, I am writing to voice my support for LD 360.
As a father of young children and a member of the Bangor School Committee, I see first-hand how critical early literacy is to their development and future success. Research shows that reading proficiency by third grade is one of the most significant indicators of a child's academic trajectory. Children who fall behind at this stage are four times more likely to drop out of high school, limiting their opportunities for higher education and future careers. The early years are crucial--not just for learning to read, but for brain development, vocabulary growth, and setting the foundation for lifelong learning. That's why I worry when I hear about declining literacy rates and the loss of programs that once supported Maine's youngest learners.
For more than 20 years, Raising Readers provided books to Maine children, but that program, along with others like it, has disappeared due to funding challenges. This has left a significant gap, making it harder for parents and educators to ensure kids have access to books at a young age. Thankfully, Dirigo Reads is stepping up, putting new books in the hands of first graders across the state. This program is already making a difference--tens of thousands of books have been distributed, and children are developing a love for reading at a critical age. But without sustainable funding, Dirigo Reads cannot reach all the students who need it most.
That's why I urge the Legislature to support funding for Dirigo Reads. Investing in early literacy isn't just the right thing to do for our kids--it's a smart economic decision. Studies show that every dollar spent on early childhood education yields up to $7 in future benefits, from higher graduation rates to increased earning potential. Other states have recognized this and committed public funds to similar programs. Maine must do the same. Our state has a proud tradition of valuing education; let's continue that legacy by ensuring every child has access to the books and resources they need to succeed.
Ben Sprague
Bangor

As a principal at Lillian P Hussey Elementary, I have witnessed firsthand the impact that access to reading materials can have on student achievement, and I believe this bill is a vital step toward improving literacy across our state.
Firstly, LD 360 proposes providing free books to students, which is essential because access to reading materials is a fundamental part of developing strong literacy skills. Research shows that students who have more books at home perform better academically and are more likely to develop a lifelong passion for reading. This bill will help bridge the gap for students who may not have access to books, giving them the opportunity to develop the critical skills they need to succeed.
Secondly, the bill's focus on ensuring that every student receives a book will not only improve literacy but also foster a sense of ownership and pride in learning. As a principal, I've seen the difference that having books students are excited about can make in their engagement and enthusiasm for reading. This bill will give students the opportunity to choose books that spark their interests, empowering them to take charge of their learning and develop a love for reading that will last a lifetime.
I strongly urge you to support this bill as it moves forward in the legislative process. Thank you for your consideration of this important issue and for your commitment to improving education in Maine.
Sincerely, Christina McDonald Principal, Lillian P Hussey Elementary School Augusta ME

Derek Perkins Superintendent of Schools, School Union #93 Board Member, Dirigo Reads 21 Horseshoe Lane, Hampden, Maine 04444 February 25, 2025
Testimony in Support of Dirigo Reads Before the State of Maine Legislature
Dear Chairperson, esteemed members of the committee,
I am honored to submit this testimony in strong support of Dirigo Reads, a nonprofit organization dedicated to fostering literacy among Maine's youth by providing every first-grade student with a new book each month. As the Superintendent of Schools for School Union #93 and a proud member of the Dirigo Reads Board of Directors, I have witnessed firsthand the profound impact this program has on our students and communities.
The ability to read proficiently is a fundamental cornerstone of academic success and lifelong opportunity. Research consistently demonstrates that early exposure to books and literacy-rich environments significantly enhances a child's cognitive development, language skills, and future academic achievements. Dirigo Reads directly addresses this critical need by ensuring that first-grade students--regardless of socioeconomic status--have access to high-quality reading materials.
In School Union #93, both the Adams School in Castine and Surry Elementary School actively participate in the Dirigo Reads program, and the results have been remarkable. Teachers report that students are more engaged with reading, demonstrate greater confidence in their literacy skills, and eagerly anticipate receiving their monthly books. Parents have shared stories of increased reading at home, fostering a culture of literacy that extends beyond the classroom. By making books accessible and exciting, Dirigo Reads not only supports academic success but also cultivates a lifelong love of reading.
The benefits of this program extend far beyond the individual student. A literate population strengthens Maine's workforce, reduces barriers to economic and social mobility, and enhances the overall well-being of our communities. Investing in early literacy is one of the most effective ways to ensure a brighter future for our state.
I urge you to support initiatives that expand and sustain the mission of Dirigo Reads. By investing in early literacy, we are investing in Maine's future. Thank you for your time and for your commitment to the education and well-being of our children.

10034662:
LD 360 Dirigo Reads Funding Testimony

February 27, 2025

Dear Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy,

and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education,

I am writing to voice my support for LD 360. My name is Elizabeth Sutherland, a business owner in Bangor and a resident of Glenburn, and I am here today as Vice President of the Board of Directors for Dirigo Reads--but more importantly, as someone who believes fiercely in the power of books to change lives.

I grew up surrounded by books. Some of my earliest memories are of getting lost in stories, turning pages by the glow of a neon green flashlight long after I was supposed to be asleep. Those books shaped me, nurtured my curiosity, and ultimately, helped me become who I am today. They taught me that words have power. They showed me new worlds, new perspectives, and endless possibilities.

But not every child in Maine has that same experience.

That's why Dirigo Reads exists.

Dirigo Reads was built on the belief that every first grader in Maine deserves to have books of their own--books they can keep, books that spark their imagination, books that make them fall in love with reading. Since the program began, thousands of books have made their way into the hands of thousands of Maine's first graders, many of whom might not otherwise have access to them.

And one of the things we've learned is that not every child falls in love with reading the same way. Some young readers get hooked by magical stories and adventures, while others prefer fact-based books that feed their curiosity about the real world. That's why Dirigo Reads provides a mix of fiction and nonfiction books--because when kids have books that truly interest them, they're far more likely to become lifelong readers.

The research is crystal clear--children who read proficiently by third grade are four times more likely to graduate high school. They go on to earn more, contribute more, and break cycles of poverty that many Maine families struggle with. Early literacy is not just about reading--it's about economic development, workforce preparedness, and the future of our state.

And yet, despite the clear educational and lifelong economic benefits of early literacy, Maine has lost some of its most impactful reading programs.

 Raising Readers--which for 20 years provided books to children at their wellness visits--is gone.
 Other early literacy initiatives have disappeared due to funding challenges.  Dirigo Reads is one of the only statewide programs left, actively working in all 16 counties to
fill that gap and give kids the foundation they need to succeed.

207-945-9999 www.sutherlandweston.com

LD 360 Dirigo Reads Funding Testimony
And the truth is--we can't do it alone. Right now, Dirigo Reads relies on generous but limited private funding to reach as many kids as possible. But there are more children who need books, more schools and communities eager to participate, and a greater need than ever for state-level support. I urge you to support this bill and help ensure that every child in Maine has not just the ability to read--but the joy of reading, and hope for a prosperous future. Thank you for your time and consideration. Sincerely,

Elizabeth Sutherland, APR

President & CEO

Sutherland Weston

Bangor ME 04401

RE: Urgent Need for State Support for Dirigo Reads Literacy Program
Dear Chairperson,
I am expressing my strong support for increased state funding for early literacy programs in Maine, particularly for Dirigo Reads, a program that provides essential books to first graders across our state. As research consistently shows, early literacy is one of the most critical factors in a child's future academic and economic success.
Reading proficiency by third grade is a key predictor of a student's long-term educational trajectory. Children who do not meet this milestone are four times more likely to drop out of high school, limiting their future opportunities and placing greater strain on social and economic systems. Early literacy enhances brain development and vocabulary and lays the groundwork for a more skilled and competitive workforce in Maine.
Unfortunately, Maine has lost several key literacy initiatives in recent years. Raising Readers, which served children for over 20 years, is no longer operating, and other community-based literacy efforts have struggled due to funding challenges. Dirigo Reads is now one of the only remaining statewide programs actively working to fill this gap, ensuring children have access to books at a critical stage of their development.
Since its launch, Dirigo Reads has distributed tens of thousands of books to first graders, fostering a love of reading and providing children with the resources they need to succeed. However, without sustained state funding, the program cannot continue to grow and meet the demand in more communities. Other states have recognized the long-term benefits of investing in early literacy and have allocated public funds to similar programs. Maine should do the same.
Investing in early literacy is not only a moral imperative--it is a smart economic decision. Research shows that every dollar spent on early childhood education yields a return of up to $7 in future benefits, including reduced remedial education costs, higher graduation rates, and increased workforce earnings. By supporting Dirigo Reads, the Legislature can ensure that all Maine children, regardless of background, can access the books they need to become strong, confident readers.

I urge you to support funding for Dirigo Reads and other early literacy initiatives to help build a stronger future for Maine. Our state has a proud tradition of valuing education--let's continue that legacy by prioritizing early literacy.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss this issue further and look forward to your support in ensuring that every child in Maine has the opportunity to thrive through the power of reading.
Sincerely, Kerri Watson-Blaisdell Vice President The County Federal Credit Union

My students look forward to their new book every month and often open them before the end of the school day. I also have students ask if they can still get a new book every month even though they are not in first grade anymore and are very disappointed when I tell them that it is for first grade only.
RSU 74 is a low income area. Many of my student's families do not have access to high quality children's books. Use of a car is not always available for all families. Usually the money for gasoline is reserved for trips to and from work. That money for gasoline would not be used to buy books or for travel to a bookstore. In our rural community, high speed internet is not always available either especially with our low income families.
Reading is vital to all children's learning. High quality books help them grow and learn. Unfortunately, not everyone knows what a high quality book is, where to find one and can afford to buy it. Please keep this great program going for as long as possible!
Thank you for your time and consideration, Solon Elementary School's First Grade.
